subject: Intermittent post-cutover connectivity — private deployment edge degradation
messages:
From: Archwell Health Ops <ops@archwell.health>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: noc@equinox.net
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: successful cutover but now intermittent TLS failures / timeouts

Hi Stephanie —

We completed the private deployment cutover to Redwood's VPC last night, but since ~08:45 PDT we’re seeing intermittent TLS handshake failures to the API and spikes in latency for a subset of requests (50-60% of requests to /v1/generate from a single aggregator host). Attach a short pcap capture and a tcpdump around the time the failures happened (archwell-pcap-snippet-0908.pcap).

Symptoms:
- Client-side: repeated TLS handshake timeout, then successful retries.
- Server-side: connection resets visible in our gateway logs, and a bunch of ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages at ~08:46.
- A subset of requests succeed with normal latency; failures look correlated to longer paths traversing Equinox transit.

Can Redwood confirm if there are known MTU/PMTU issues on the private link? We also observed ephemeral port exhaustion warnings on our NAT appliance around the same time (vendor logs). This is urgent for our customer-facing traffic — can we get a triage owner and next steps?

Thanks,
Laura Park
SRE, Archwell Health
ops@archwell.health

Hi Laura — I’m stepping in to coordinate. Sorry you’re seeing this after cutover. I’ve looped in our Private Deploy and Network teams (Vanessa, Karthik, Rishi, Connor), and copied Equinox NOC for transit visibility.

Immediate asks:
- Laura: can you share a short traceroute to the failing backend IPs and the exact client IPs that show failures? The pcap is helpful — can you also include one tcpdump showing the TLS SYN/SYN-ACK/FIN pattern around a failure?
- Equinox: can you confirm whether you’re seeing ICMP "fragmentation needed"/PMTU signals for flows between Archwell and Redwood edge?

Our plan (provisional): quick triage call in 30m if helpful, collect traceroutes/pcap/flow logs, then validate for asymmetric routing, SNAT port availability, and any MTU black-holing.

I’ll open a Jira and post a summary here.

-Stephanie

JIRA created: RED-4821

From: Equinox NOC <noc@equinox.net>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Archwell Health Ops <ops@archwell.health>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: successful cutover but now intermittent TLS failures / timeouts

Hi all — we see a brief burst of ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) originating from a hop inside the Equinox transit for a small percentage of connections between Archwell's aggregator IP block and Redwood edge (traced via our edge: 198.51.100.22 -> 203.0.113.57 -> 198.51.100.1).

We ran a quick traceroute and attach the output (equinox-trace-0905.txt). BGP is stable; we haven’t seen withdraws. However, PMTU discovery is failing in some paths — the DF bit set by some clients is causing discards on a downstream hop that does not send proper ICMP responses back (we see asymmetric return paths for ICMP).

Suggested immediate mitigations from our side: we can temporarily enable MSS clamping at our egress toward the affected path and surface any ICMP errors to you. That will reduce MTU mismatch impact while you investigate NAT/port use and your on-prem firewall behaviour.

-NOC Team
Equinox Transit

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: successful cutover but now intermittent TLS failures / timeouts

Team — quick dump of what we’re seeing from the Redwood side after pulling flow logs and conntrack samples (attached: redwood-flowlogs-aggregate.csv). Summary:
- A cluster of flows from Archwell's aggregator (203.0.113.0/28) show return packets taking a different egress (asymmetry) that routes back through a partner leg where ICMP responses get dropped.
- There are several ephemeral port collisions in our SNAT pools for the egress path at ~08:45 (we log port reuse warnings on the SNAT allocator). That correlates with retries from the client side and the TLS timeouts.
- MTU signature: we see ICMP frag-needed hits on one partner transit but not seeing corresponding ICMP back to the original source due to an asymmetric hop.

Immediate recommended actions:
1) Ask Archwell to add MSS clamping on their aggregator (or remove DF for that overlay) — quick fix.
2) We will request Equinox to enable MSS clamping on the transit leg (if they can) as fallback.
3) Short-term: increase SNAT ephemeral port range for the affected pool by 2x and add a conservative conntrack timeout for SYN_RECV windows to avoid port reuse under load.
4) Longer-term: work with Archwell to normalize PMTU responses; review on-prem firewall for ICMP filtering and NAT appliance port allocation.

Attaching two CSVs and a conntrack excerpt in the drive link. I can take lead on the SNAT/conntrack change — need Vanessa or Connor to approve change window.

-karthik
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: successful cutover but now intermittent TLS failures / timeouts

Thanks — we ran a couple more captures and confirmed the pattern. The attached pcap shows MSS advertised at 1500 from hosts, but along the path a downstream hop is effectively limiting payload to ~1420 (we see fragmentation-needed and then no ICMP reply to the sender because of asymmetry). We will push an MSS clamp on the aggregator firewall this morning and coordinate with our NAT vendor to verify ephemeral port sizing; they reported the appliance default range is small for high-flow NAT.

We’re ok with Redwood increasing the SNAT port range as a temporary mitigation — please advise expected impact to session count and whether that requires a maintenance window. If we can get both endpoints clamping and an increase on your SNAT, we’ll validate and revert if stable.

Attached: archwell-pcap-snippet-0908.pcap (detailed)

-Laura
SRE, Archwell Health

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Archwell Health Ops <ops@archwell.health>, Equinox NOC <noc@equinox.net>

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: successful cutover but now intermittent TLS failures / timeouts — agreed actions

Thanks everyone — summary and owners: 

1) Archwell (Laura): apply MSS clamp at aggregator firewall (target: MTU 1420) and confirm tcpdump after change (owner: Archwell Ops).
2) Equinox NOC: enable temporary MSS clamping on the transit leg toward 203.0.113.0/28 for the next 3 hours and monitor (owner: Equinox).
3) Redwood (Karthik): temporarily increase SNAT ephemeral port range for the affected egress pool and add conservative conntrack SYN timeouts. I will schedule change at 14:15 PDT and roll back if no impact (owner: Karthik; approver: Vanessa).
4) Redwood (Connor/Rishi): run a post-change validation checklist — traceroute, flowlog comparison, and client-request success rate sampling; post results to RED-4821.

Operational notes: this is an active customer-facing degradation; we should keep the channel open until both endpoints confirm stability for 1 hour. Vanessa — can you approve the 14:15 SNAT window?

Thanks — I’ll keep the Jira updated and capture the postmortem items (SNAT sizing, PMTU hardening playbook, and documentation for on-prem partners).

-Stephanie
Product Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
